resolutions.resolution: we will use the flat tree in section 6.2.1
resolutions.background: Emilio pointed me out the the spec should use the flat tree rather than DOM tree. I agree with him, the flat tree would be more intuitive for web developers.
irc: <kbabbitt> emilio: this is about which tree order we use to select snap points
<kbabbitt> ... the spec seems to use dom order
<TabAtkins> q+
<kbabbitt> ... but I think that doesn't make any sense, because dom order and layout tree order don't have anything to do with each other once you ? slots
<kbabbitt> ... I think spec should just use flat tree order, that's what Firefox does
<kbabbitt> ... we haven't seen any compat issues
<kbabbitt> ... also how things like counters work
<flackr> q+
<astearns> ack TabAtkins
<kbabbitt> TabAtkins: just to understand a little better, is this ordering only being used for telling which element we're snapping to when multiple snap points coincide?
<kbabbitt> emilio: it's been a while, need to look at test, but yes I think so
<kbabbitt> TabAtkins: so this is just tie breaking... I don't have a strong opinion, whatever works better for implementations works for me
<kbabbitt> ... no correct answer, just a matter of selecting a winner out of otherwise indistinguishable possibilities
<kbabbitt> ... unlike e.g. counters where order is visible and smantic
<kbabbitt> ... less obvious what the answer should be here
<astearns> ack flackr
<kbabbitt> flackr: TabAtkins already asked the question I wanted to
<kbabbitt> ... I think I agree that using flat tree makes more sense
<kbabbitt> astearns: proposed resolution is to use the flat tree in ... what exactly?
<kbabbitt> [missed]
<kbabbitt> flackr: it's in the scroll snap spec when choosing between equally valid candidates
<kbabbitt> astearns: proposed, we will use the flat tree in section 6.2.1
<kbabbitt> RESOLVED: we will use the flat tree in section 6.2.1

resolutions.resolution: we will do reversals of static positions in grid-lanes
resolutions.background: In the case we are using fill-reverse on a grid-lanes container (ie either `grid-lanes-direction: row fill-reverse` or `grid-lanes-direction: column fill-reverse`), do we expect the static positions of the out-of-flow items to be reversed along the stacking axis as well?
irc: <kbabbitt> cepan: context is, in grid-lanes container, if fill-reverse is applied, we fill from end of stacking axis
<kbabbitt> ... columns that's bottom to top, rows right to left
<kbabbitt> ... question is, if we have out of flow items, do we want to change their static positions?
<kbabbitt> ... if we change the flow usig fill reverse seems like static positions should be affected as well
<kbabbitt> ... there's a follow up question for track reverse case
<kbabbitt> ... where in columns you fill from right to left
<kbabbitt> ... do we want to reverse static positions in track reverse case as well?
<kbabbitt> ... my suggestion was for both fill-reverse and track-reverse, yes we do want to adjust static positions
<kbabbitt> astearns: and you note we do reverse static positions in flex?
<emilio> q+
<kbabbitt> cepan: in flex we do reverse static positions with any reversals
<astearns> ack emilio
<TabAtkins> I have no strong opinion on static positions (in general I think non-block static positions are more or less useless), so I'm happy to go with whatever's consistent and easy
<kbabbitt> emilio: don't disagree necessarily, was going to make a simmilar comment
<kbabbitt> ... generally we try to keep static positions as simple as possible
<TabAtkins> yeah +1 to emilio
<kbabbitt> ... if this is simple implementation wise then it's fair
<kbabbitt> ... otherwise I feel either way would be okay
<kbabbitt> ... is there a ? static position to choose if we don't reverse otherwise?
<kbabbitt> ... so you're laying stuff out, you hit an abspos
<kbabbitt> ... if you don't reverse them, is there a good way to come up with a reasonable static position? 0,0 or something?
<TabAtkins> q+
<kbabbitt> cepan: yes, I think static position is where it would be without other reversals
<kbabbitt> ... it's possible item ends up far away
<fantasai> I think I agree with the static position being flow-responsive
<TabAtkins> one sec
<kbabbitt> TabAtkins: in general I find static positions outside block layout to be more ore less useless
<kbabbitt> ... what static position does in block layout does not represent a useful position in grid, flex, etc.
<kbabbitt> ... like emilio said I'm fine with anything that is simple and consisitent
<kbabbitt> ... don't need to worry about use cases, there aren't any for static positions in these things
<astearns> ack TabAtkins
<kbabbitt> ... as long as we have something that's reasonably consistent and explainable I'm fine with anything we come up with
<kbabbitt> astearns: don't think there is a reversal case in non-lanes grid, is that the case?
<kbabbitt> fantasai: if we add reversal to grid-lanes, we should add to grid as well, we have an outstanding resolution for that
<kbabbitt> ... so there will be reversals in all 3 layouts
<kbabbitt> astearns: so I see 2 ways forward. one is, don't mess with it because we don't think anyone will use it, other is, do reversals because we have a precedent in flexbox
<kbabbitt> cepan: I think it makes sense to follow flexbox precedent
<kbabbitt> ... if no one has any objections, I'd prefer that
<sgill> +1
<TabAtkins> +1
<hoch> +1
<kbabbitt> astearns: I think I'm in that camp as well
<kbabbitt> ... proposed resolution is we will do reversals of static positions in grid-lanes
<kbabbitt> RESOLVED: we will do reversals of static positions in grid-lanes

<kbabbitt> ... spec talks about how to do this for svg elements but not css boxes
<kbabbitt> ... impls have converged on using ink overflow bounds for userSpaceOnUse, ? for objectBoundingBOx
<kbabbitt> ... this matters because you could create SVG filters for things with flood which identify extent of ink overflow

resolutions.resolution: Snap positions affect the nearest ancestor scroll container in each axis they align to
resolutions.background: One of the questions is whether scroll snap also tracks per-axis scrollers. I think that would be reasonable. One hiccup is that [`scroll-snap-type`](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-scroll-snap/#scroll-snap-type) includes an axis in which this scroller snaps.
irc: <kbabbitt> vmpstr: we have resolved to be able to create single axis scrollers by not coercing overflow clip into hidden
<kbabbitt> ... when the other axis is something like scroll
<kbabbitt> ... this means that the element becomes a scroller in one axis but not the other
<kbabbitt> ... TabAtkins put together a draft PR to update a bunch of specs for this
<TabAtkins> (no longer a draft PR, it's merged now)
<kbabbitt> ... a lot of cases you have to find nearest scroll container and which axis matters
<kbabbitt> ... this issue is about scroll-snap
<kbabbitt> ... I think we want to say it's reasonable to want to snap 2 different scrollers for 2 different axes
<kbabbitt> ... one smallproblem here is that scroller, when it specifies snap type, also specifies an axis
<kbabbitt> ... question is what do we do in these cases
<kbabbitt> ... think it's obvious for vertical scroller with vertical axis
<TabAtkins> definitely +1 to the proposal in the issue, it's consistent with the non-scrolling behavior and how we treat single-axis scrollers elsewhere
<kbabbitt> ... question is what do we do if we have a vertical scroller with snap in horizontal axis
<kbabbitt> ... proposal I have is that we ignore the fact that scroll-snap-type has horizontal axis since scroller is not horizontal
<kbabbitt> ... would find scroller higher up
<kbabbitt> ... examp[les in the issue
<kbabbitt> flackr: this is the same as what we do for scroll-snap-type on non-scroller
<kbabbitt> vmpstr: right, first we find a scroller then check its scroll-snap-type
<kbabbitt> astearns: questions or concerns?
<flackr> +1 to the proposal
<smfr> q+
<TabAtkins> non-scrolling axises don't capture snaps
<kbabbitt> vmpstr: scroll-snap-type which doesn't affect a scroller doesn't contribute scroll points
<kbabbitt> smfr: if you have nested scrollers and inner scroller is horizontal, when you're selecting snap candidates in parent scroller, you are looking at ones in inner scroller?
<kbabbitt> vmpstr: the ones for other axis, yes
<kbabbitt> smfr: when you specify a snap target, do you give it an axis?
<kbabbitt> flackr: yes, you specify scroll-snap-align in each axis
<kbabbitt> smfr: guess that makes sense
<kbabbitt> astearns: this makes sense to me but summary in minutes doesn't yet
<kbabbitt> ... when there's a mismatch between scroll-snap-type and scroll axes, we ignore the mismatched scroller?
<kbabbitt> vmpstr: essentially you do bitwise and between scroll-snap-type axis and which axis the element is a scroller
<flackr> Proposed resolution: Snap positions affect the nearest ancestor scroll container in each axis they align to
<kbabbitt> ... if it has both but scroller is only vertical only consider snapping in vertical axis, horizontal snap can be in ancestor scroller
<flackr> existing spec text is "Snap positions only affect the nearest ancestor scroll container on the element’s containing block chain."
<TabAtkins> yeah +1 to resolution
<kbabbitt> flackr: wrote a resolution based on existing spec text
<kbabbitt> ... I am proposing that we just say "in each axis which they align to"
<ChrisL> +1
<kbabbitt> astearns: right because really we are affecting scrolling of scroll container based on what scroll positions
<kbabbitt> astearns: any objections to flackr's proposed resolution?
<kbabbitt> RESOLVED: Snap positions affect the nearest ancestor scroll container in each axis they align to
